module_title: Advanced Analysis - Strategic Reserves, CBM, and the Gas Grid
introduction: This advanced level analyzes India's energy security strategies, specifically focusing on how the country prepares for global supply shocks. We will also explore emerging, unconventional energy extractions like Coal Bed Methane, the massive discoveries in the eastern offshore basins, and the government's vision to transition toward a gas-based economy.

core_concepts.title: Strategic Petroleum Reserves (SPR)
core_concepts.description: Because India imports over 80% of its crude oil requirements, it is highly vulnerable to global supply chain disruptions (like wars or blockades). To ensure energy security, the Indian Strategic Petroleum Reserves Ltd (ISPRL) has built massive underground rock caverns to store emergency crude oil. These operational facilities are strategically located in coastal areas: Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh), Mangaluru (Karnataka), and Padur (Karnataka).

core_concepts.title: Coal Bed Methane (CBM)
core_concepts.description: CBM is an unconventional form of natural gas found trapped within coal seams. Unlike traditional natural gas, which is found in sandstone or porous rocks, CBM is adsorbed into the solid matrix of the coal itself. Because India has the 5th largest proven coal reserves in the world, extracting CBM offers a massive, untapped domestic clean energy source that can significantly reduce our reliance on imported liquefied natural gas (LNG).

core_concepts.title: Krishna-Godavari (KG) Basin
core_concepts.description: While Mumbai High dominates the western coast, the Krishna-Godavari Basin located on the eastern coast (offshore Andhra Pradesh) has emerged as the most critical new frontier for energy exploration. Massive reserves of natural gas (like the famous KG-D6 block) have been discovered here, fundamentally shifting India's energy map from the west coast to include the east coast.

core_concepts.title: One Nation, One Gas Grid
core_concepts.description: This is a flagship government initiative aimed at connecting all corners of India through a unified, massive network of natural gas pipelines. The goal is to shift India towards a 'gas-based economy' by increasing the share of natural gas in the energy mix from the current 6% to 15%. This will help reduce severe urban pollution caused by coal and liquid transport fuels.

important_entities.name: Barauni and Mathura Refineries
important_entities.description: Most oil refineries are built on the coast (like Jamnagar or Kochi) to easily receive imported crude oil via ships. However, Barauni (Bihar) and Mathura (UP) are significant because they are 'inland' refineries. They were built deep inside the country, near massive consumer markets, and they rely entirely on thousands of kilometers of pipelines to receive their raw crude oil.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Shale Gas vs. Coal Bed Methane
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Do not confuse these two unconventional gases in Assertion-Reasoning questions. 'Shale Gas' is trapped in fine-grained sedimentary rocks (shale) and requires highly controversial 'hydraulic fracturing' (fracking) to extract. 'Coal Bed Methane' is trapped directly inside coal seams and is generally extracted by pumping water out of the coal bed to depressurize it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Remember the three existing underground rock cavern sites for emergency oil storage: Visakhapatnam (V), Mangaluru (M), and Padur (P).

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC heavily targets the 'KG Basin'. If a question asks about the largest recent discoveries of Natural Gas in India, the answer is almost always the Krishna-Godavari Basin.

Understand the geographic logic: Coastal refineries are 'Port-based' (to minimize raw material transport costs), while inland refineries are 'Market-based' (to minimize finished product distribution costs).
